subject: Developer tool renewals: proposed license consolidation & negotiation plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Developer tool renewals: proposed license consolidation & negotiation plan

Team —

We have a cluster of renewals coming up in Q3 for core developer tooling (GitHub Enterprise, JetBrains All Products Pack, Atlassian cloud seats for Jira/Confluence). I pulled the attached inventory and high-level spend (see 2026-05-20_devtools_inventory.xlsx).

Primary asks:
- Decide whether we pursue a single-vendor consolidated negotiation (one P.O. + enterprise agreement) vs. separate renewals.
- Identify any hard requirements for seat counts / SSO/KMS / audit log retention per team.
- Confirm owners for negotiation threads (I'll coordinate procurement + legal once we pick approach).

My initial read: consolidating conversations will strengthen our bargaining position (volume discounts + unified SLAs), but timing is tricky — GitHub renewal window starts mid-July, JetBrains in early August, Atlassian late July. If we aim to overlap negotiation windows we need to commit to scope by mid-June.

Please reply with: 1) your recommended path (consolidate | staggered), 2) any non-negotiable constraints, 3) quick estimate of required seats (if different from the spreadsheet).

Karthik
Director, Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-05-20_devtools_inventory.xlsx (spreadsheet - inventory + current spend)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Developer tool renewals: proposed license consolidation & negotiation plan

Thanks Karthik — quick responses below.

Recommended path: consolidate conversations where possible, but negotiate GitHub separately if needed for enterprise features (GH Advanced Security and SAML auditing are on different timelines).

Seats / constraints (engineering org):
- GitHub Enterprise: current active seats ~420 (spreadsheet shows 400; we added teams from Platform and LLM infra). Will need +20 seats but we can convert inactive seats first.
- JetBrains APM: ~185 seats across backend/mobile/frontend. We have 3 team leads requesting remote license portability (we prefer per-user but with floating seat pool for contractors).
- Atlassian (Jira/Confluence): 520 users across product and CS; storage and retention are the main asks — we need 2-year audit log retention for compliance.

Non-negotiables: GitHub Advanced Security enablement for infra and SRE; Atlassian audit retention as above. JetBrains — willing to consider a 1-year term with a price cap.

Happy to own GitHub side, can run initial usage analytics and walk the vendor through our GHAS requirements.

Laura
VP, Product Engineering
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Developer tool renewals: proposed license consolidation & negotiation plan

Karthik / Laura —

Agree on consolidating vendor conversations where it makes sense; procurement likes single-touchpoint for approvals. A few Atlassian-specific notes:
- Current Atlassian contract auto-renews on 2026-07-28. We have early-termination penalties if we change billing cadence; need legal review.
- The finance team is pushing to move Atlassian to annual pre-pay to capture a 10% discount — that requires final seat count locked 30 days prior.
- We have a list of 27 guest accounts and service accounts that are currently counted as users; we should clean these up to reduce counts before we lock.

If we consolidate negotiations, I recommend:
1) Lock GitHub scope first (Laura to lead) — GitHub has the most complex feature gating.
2) Parallel asks to JetBrains & Atlassian: request enterprise-level discounts and multi-year caps.
3) Procurement runs a single negotiation calendar and routes quotes through legal (I can coordinate approvals once contracts are ready).

I'll run a quick cleanup pass on the Atlassian roster and share the before/after seat counts by 6/07.

Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations (also managing procurement workflows)
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Developer tool renewals: proposed license consolidation & negotiation plan

All —

I ran a quick procurement feasibility check with finance. Key items:
- Consolidation yields better leverage but adds workflow complexity (one legal review covering three different vendor T&Cs). Finance prefers separate P.O.s for each vendor for accounting clarity, but is open to dealer consolidation if we get multi-year price guarantees and clear invoice rollups.
- Budget cycle: approvals for Q3 spend need to be submitted by 7/10. If we plan any multi-year commitments we should model cashflow for FY27.

Practical recommendation: proceed with a hybrid approach — Laura runs GitHub negotiation immediately (because GHAS and renewal date), procurement opens parallel RFP threads with JetBrains and Atlassian but requests hold pricing and a 30-day lock (expiration mid-June). If pricing looks favorable, we move to consolidated PO for discount capture.

Grace
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Rao <priya@jetbrains.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: JetBrains: updated enterprise quote and floating seat proposal

Hi Karthik / Laura / team —

Thanks for the heads up and the inventory sheet. Attached is an updated quote (jetbrains_quote_v2.pdf) that includes:
- 3% volume discount at 200+ seats
- Floating seat pool of 30 licenses for contractors (applies to All Products Pack)
- One-year term with renewal cap at +5%

We can hold this pricing until 2026-06-20 if you confirm headcount and provide SSO integration details. We also included a note on exporter licensing for remote users (see page 3).

Next steps suggested:
1) Confirm seat counts and floating seat enrollment by 6/18.
2) Provide SSO issuer URL and SCIM provisioning contact for our integration team.
3) Let us know if you prefer a multi-year term — we can propose a 2-year agreement with a steeper discount but would need a signed MSA.

Happy to hop on a short call next week to walk through the quote.

Best,
Priya Rao
Enterprise Accounts — JetBrains
priya@jetbrains.com

Attachments: jetbrains_quote_v2.pdf (PDF - enterprise quote)
